newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnia local polls hit new snags.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia local polls hit new snags.

text.p: Intense diplomatic efforts have so far failed to resolve an impasse threatening Bosnian local elections due next month, while international agencies have clashed over their electoral responsibilities.

The Serbs have said they could boycott the polls because of rising tension in some areas of Bosnia and dissatisfaction with the international body running the elections, the Organisation for Cooperation and Security in Europe (OSCE).
Carl Bildt, the international community's High Representative in Bosnia, told the OSCE it must take not shirk its responsibility for ensuring that successful candidates are able to take up office.
In a letter to OSCE chief Flavio Cotti, Bildt said the elections should not be considered in isolation.
"There has to be a responsibility for implementing their results," the letter said.

"The local elections represent a major challenge for the entire peace implementation efforts. The way this challenge is handled will be one of the most significant factors affecting the results of the international efforts in this country."
OSCE spokesman David Foley said the OSCE had some reservations about whether the installation of candidates was part of its mandate, but it was working to resolve the issue with Bildt's office.
Ensuring elected candidates are able to take up office in sensitive areas of Bosnia has emerged as one of the key issues facing the peace process in the former Yugoslav republic.
Commenting on efforts to overcome the Serbs' objections to the local elections, Foley said consultations continued over the weekend and while progress had been made, no agreement had been reached.

Discussions had been held with officials close to Biljana Plavsic, the hardline President of the Serb republic in Bosnia, to try to persuade her to drop her opposition to OSCE-supervised municipal elections set for November 23 and 24.
"It is an intensive diplomatic exercise. We are consulting, coordinating and cooperating with all sides," Foley told a news conference.
"We believe that things are moving in the right direction but we have not reached closure on the issue."

Foley said the OSCE's Bosnian mission chief, Robert Frowick of the United States, still wanted to hold the elections as planned, and issued a warning that postponement could mean the polls might have to be held without international supervision.
"Postponement is under any circumstances unlikely," Foley said.
"The choice is to hold municipal elections now, as scheduled, under international supervision or there is a risk that they will not be held at all under international supervision," he said.
The local elections follow national polls for a presidency and parliament held on September 14.
